n: John Brown Farm State Historic Site
w: Abolitionist John Brown moved to this farm in 1849 to teach farming to African American settlers, and it remains his final resting place. Once called the highest arable land in New York, its panorama was said to outshine even nearby Mirror Lake. State-managed since 1896, it became a National Historic Landmark in 1998.
s: John Brown's farm and grave, highest arable land in NY
_facts: John Brown moved here in 1849 to teach farming to African American settlers
Called "the highest arable spot of land" in New York State
State-managed since 1896; National Historic Landmark since 1998

w: A temporary stadium built alongside this permanent equestrian venue held 30,000 spectators for the opening ceremonies of the 1980 Winter Olympics - one of two Winter Games Lake Placid has hosted, the only US village to do so before Salt Lake City's 2034 turn.
s: Opening-ceremony site of the 1980 Winter Olympics
_facts: Temporary stadium built alongside it held 30,000 spectators for the 1980 opening ceremonies
Part of Lake Placid's Olympic venue cluster (host of both 1932 and 1980 Games)

w: Built for the 1980 Winter Olympics alongside the USA Rink, this arena is named for Herb Brooks, coach of the US hockey team that upset the Soviet Union here in the 'Miracle on Ice' - a game whose relics now fill the nearby Lake Placid Winter Olympic Museum. The rink remains part of the village's Olympic Center complex.
s: Rink of the US hockey team's 1980 'Miracle on Ice'
_facts: Built for the 1980 Winter Olympics alongside the USA Rink
Named for coach Herb Brooks of the US Olympic hockey team
Site of the 'Miracle on Ice' upset of the Soviet Union
Part of the Lake Placid Olympic Center

w: This 124-acre lake sits at the center of Lake Placid village, distinct from the larger lake that gave the village its name. It reaches a maximum depth of 65 feet, averaging just 14, in a watershed that is 51 percent forest and just a fifth open water.
s: Village-center lake, distinct from its Olympic namesake
_facts: 124-acre lake in the center of Lake Placid village
Maximum depth 65 feet, average depth 14 feet
Distinct from the larger Lake Placid lake nearby

w: Opened by New York State in 1994, this museum inside the Olympic Center holds the Fram III bobsled from 1932 - missing over sixty years before its donation - plus Jack Shea's 1932 skates and memorabilia from the 1980 'Miracle on Ice' hockey team. It won the IOC's Olympic Cup in 2005.
s: Bobsleds, skates and Miracle-on-Ice relics on display
_facts: Opened 1994 by New York State inside the Olympic Center
Holds the Fram III bobsled from 1932, missing over 60 years before donation
Jack Shea's 1932 skates and 1980 'Miracle on Ice' memorabilia
Won the IOC's Olympic Cup in 2005
